title: Predicting Inventory Scaling
problem: System latency spikes during peak seasonal inventory updates when processing thousands of product SKU records.
solution: Applying Big O Notation to evaluate the asymptotic upper bound on growth for search and update algorithms, ensuring the chosen data structures maintain predictable performance as the product catalog size (n) increases.
steps: Identify the core operation, such as searching for a specific SKU in the inventory list.
Determine the worst-case scenario for the algorithm, representing the maximum number of operations required as n grows.
Express the growth rate using Big O notation to define the asymptotic upper bound.
Compare different algorithmic approaches to select one with a lower complexity class, such as O(log n) instead of O(n).
Validate that the chosen algorithm remains efficient as the total number of SKUs scales.
outcome: Stable system response times regardless of the total number of items in the inventory database.
limitation: Big O notation focuses on asymptotic behavior, which ignores constant factors; a theoretically slower algorithm might perform faster in practice for small datasets due to lower overhead.

questions.question: In Predicting Inventory Scaling, what is a key limitation of using Big O notation?
options: It is only useful for very small datasets.
It ignores constant factors, which can impact performance for small datasets.
It requires expensive hardware to implement.
It is impossible to calculate for modern systems.
questions.explanation: Big O is an asymptotic measure, meaning it describes behavior as n approaches infinity, potentially ignoring constant overhead that matters at smaller scales.
